meta.title: Shakespearean Insults — complete sourced corpus
meta.description: The faithful canon. Every entry is drawn from a verified line in Shakespeare's plays and tagged with play, act.scene, and speaker. NOTHING is deleted for taste. Filtering is the engine's job, not the data's: each entry carries a `flags` array, and the engine surfaces or withholds entries by whatever policy the host application sets. An empty `flags` array means no content advisory applies.
meta.filteringModel: Do not strip the corpus. The engine takes an allowed/blocked flag set and filters at runtime. Default presets are the host's call. This keeps the literary text whole and puts editorial control in the application layer where it belongs.

flagVocabulary.coarse: vulgar but not targeting a protected class (e.g. whoreson, fat-guts)
flagVocabulary.sexual: sexual degradation or sexual slur (e.g. strumpet, Winchester goose)
flagVocabulary.colonial: abuse of the colonized/enslaved figure (Tempest's Caliban)
flagVocabulary.violent: boast of or threat of bodily harm

tiers.note: Three sensitivity presets. An entry is permitted in a tier when every flag it carries is in that tier's allowedFlags (entries with no flags are always permitted). The 'full' tier allows all flags, so the literary text passes through UNALTERED. Flag-to-tier assignment is editorial and data-driven: reassign any flag to any tier here without touching engine code.

safe.label: Safe
safe.description: Clean entries only. No content advisories of any kind.

edgy.label: Edgy
edgy.description: Bawdy, crude, and pointed — period insults that sting or target individuals, short of modern racial/ethnic/religious slurs.

full.label: Full Offense
full.description: The unaltered canon. Includes racial and colonial material as Shakespeare wrote it. A study of the literature; output is not modified. Gated to viewers 18 or older.

epigraph.text: You taught me language, and my profit on't is, I know how to curse.
epigraph.speaker: Caliban
epigraph.note: Pinned epigraph. Display only — never enter any random pool.

meterModes.note: Meter is a per-term string: w=weak, S=strong, x=flexible monosyllable (promoted or demoted by position, as in real scansion). The engine scans an assembled candidate against a template, treating x as a wildcard. Compound adjectives whose parts are monosyllables resolve as flexible by design; a future pass may pin compound primary stress for stricter scansion.

iambicPentameter.template: wSwSwSwSwS (10) ; feminine ending allows trailing w (11)
iambicPentameter.lineForm: Thou {adj} {adj} {noun}. — 'Thou' is the opening weak beat.
iambicPentameter.authentic: permits initial trochee, one spondee or pyrrhic substitution, and feminine ending

trochaicTetrameter.template: SwSwSwSw (8) ; catalectic drops final w -> SwSwSwS (7)
trochaicTetrameter.lineForm: {Adj} {adj} {noun}! — DROP 'Thou'; trochaic lines open on a stress.
trochaicTetrameter.note: The incantation/curse meter (the witches, Puck, the fairies). Best fit for the trochaic insult-compounds.

ending.masculine: line ends on a stress — hard landing (recommended for insults)

comicNonCanonical.warning: NOT characteristically Shakespearean — limerick/Seuss register. Expose only behind a clearly-labeled comic setting.

meta.authorshipNotes: Corpus follows the modern expanded canon. Edward III (printed anonymously 1596) is now widely accepted as at least partly Shakespeare's; the Countess of Salisbury scenes are the portion most attributed to him. Several included plays are collaborative or disputed (Pericles, The Two Noble Kinsmen, Henry VIII, Timon, Titus). Edward III's invective is chiefly the Countess's contempt for the Scots (1.2), which is ethnic and flagged accordingly.

lines.text: Thou art a boil, a plague-sore, or embossed carbuncle, in my corrupted blood.
lines.speaker: King Lear
lines.gloss: A father naming his own daughter an infection in his blood.

lines.text: A knave, a rascal, an eater of broken meats.
lines.speaker: Kent
lines.gloss: Opening salvo of the longest insult in the canon.

lines.text: Thou whoreson zed! thou unnecessary letter!
lines.speaker: Kent
lines.gloss: A whole man reduced to the most useless letter in the alphabet.

lines.text: Why, thou clay-brained guts, thou knotty-pated fool.
lines.speaker: Prince Hal
lines.gloss: A skull packed with mud, and tangled wood for thought.

lines.text: That stuffed cloak-bag of guts.
lines.speaker: Prince Hal
lines.gloss: A travelling case crammed with offal, walking about.

lines.text: Peace, ye fat-guts!
lines.speaker: Prince Hal
lines.gloss: Short, and to the point.

lines.text: His wit's as thick as Tewkesbury mustard.
lines.speaker: Falstaff
lines.gloss: Thick, and good for nothing but to make the eyes water.

lines.text: Away, you scullion! you rampallian! you fustilarian! I'll tickle your catastrophe!
lines.speaker: the Page
lines.gloss: Three coined insults and a threat to your backside.

lines.text: Thou hast no more brain than I have in mine elbows.
lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.gloss: The wit is somewhere. It is not in the head.

lines.text: Thou crusty batch of nature, what's the news?
lines.speaker: Achilles
lines.gloss: A half-baked loaf God forgot to finish.

lines.text: Why, thou full dish of fool, from Troy.
lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.gloss: A heaping serving plate, brimful of idiot.

lines.text: Thou mongrel beef-witted lord!
lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.gloss: A muddle-bred ox in a coronet.

lines.text: Would thou wert clean enough to spit upon!
lines.speaker: Timon
lines.gloss: Too foul even to be the target of contempt.

lines.text: Thou art the cap of all the fools alive.
lines.speaker: Apemantus
lines.gloss: The crowning fool the rest look up to.

lines.text: A plague on thee! Thou art too bad to curse.
lines.speaker: Apemantus
lines.gloss: Beyond the reach of even a good curse.

lines.text: What's the matter, you dissentious rogues, that, rubbing the poor itch of your opinion, make yourselves scabs?
lines.speaker: Coriolanus
lines.gloss: Scratch an opinion long enough and you become the sore.

lines.text: You common cry of curs! whose breath I hate as reek o' the rotten fens.
lines.speaker: Coriolanus
lines.gloss: A pack of yapping dogs whose breath is swamp-gas.

lines.text: You souls of geese, that bear the shapes of men!
lines.speaker: Coriolanus
lines.gloss: Men-shaped, but honking and witless inside.

lines.text: Boy! False hound!
lines.speaker: Coriolanus
lines.gloss: One syllable, detonating a war hero.

lines.text: Excellent well; you are a fishmonger.
lines.speaker: Hamlet
lines.gloss: The insult lands on the audience; Polonius never catches it.

lines.text: O, what a rogue and peasant slave am I!
lines.speaker: Hamlet
lines.gloss: The sharpest tongue in the play, turned inward.

lines.text: Remorseless, treacherous, lecherous, kindless villain!
lines.speaker: Hamlet
lines.gloss: Four hammer-blows and a verdict.

lines.text: A king of shreds and patches.
lines.speaker: Hamlet
lines.gloss: A king stitched together from rags.

lines.text: The devil damn thee black, thou cream-faced loon!
lines.speaker: Macbeth
lines.gloss: White with fear, and damned for it in the same breath.

lines.text: Go prick thy face and over-red thy fear, thou lily-livered boy!
lines.speaker: Macbeth
lines.gloss: Bleed some courage into that pale face.

lines.text: Turn, hell-hound, turn!
lines.speaker: Macduff
lines.gloss: Three words, and a reckoning behind them.

lines.text: You blocks, you stones, you worse than senseless things!
lines.speaker: Marullus
lines.gloss: Less responsive than the paving stones they stand on.

lines.text: Away, slight man!
lines.speaker: Brutus
lines.gloss: Dismissal between equals, which stings worse than rage.

lines.text: Rogue, thou hast lived too long!
lines.speaker: Cleopatra
lines.gloss: A death sentence as a greeting.

lines.text: Thou shalt be whipped with wire and stewed in brine, smarting in lingering pickle.
lines.speaker: Cleopatra
lines.gloss: A three-stage culinary torture, promised.

lines.text: Hadst thou Narcissus in thy face, to me thou wouldst appear most ugly.
lines.speaker: Cleopatra
lines.gloss: Even at your best you'd still be hideous.

lines.text: I have done a thousand dreadful things as willingly as one would kill a fly.
lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.gloss: Atrocity recited as a résumé.

lines.text: If one good deed in all my life I did, I do repent it from my very soul.
lines.speaker: Aaron
lines.gloss: Unrepentant to the last syllable.

lines.text: Rome is but a wilderness of tigers.
lines.speaker: Titus
lines.gloss: A whole city named a beast-pit.

lines.text: Tybalt, you rat-catcher, will you walk?
lines.speaker: Mercutio
lines.gloss: A goad, not a curse — a dare wrapped in a cat joke.

lines.text: Good King of Cats, nothing but one of your nine lives.
lines.speaker: Mercutio
lines.gloss: Mocking Tybalt's name to his face.

lines.text: Out, you green-sickness carrion! Out, you baggage! You tallow-face!
lines.speaker: Capulet
lines.gloss: A pale-faced run of scorn: anemic, worthless, waxen.

lines.text: You are a princox, go!
lines.speaker: Capulet
lines.gloss: A cocky young upstart, told to sit down.

lines.text: You loggerheaded and unpolished grooms!
lines.speaker: Petruchio
lines.gloss: Blockheads, and rough-cut ones at that.

lines.text: A whoreson, beetle-headed, flap-eared knave!
lines.speaker: Petruchio
lines.gloss: Head like a mallet, ears like flaps.

lines.text: Thou thread, thou thimble, thou nit, thou winter-cricket thou!
lines.speaker: Petruchio
lines.gloss: A man reduced to a pile of sewing-room scraps.

lines.text: Away, thou rag, thou quantity, thou remnant!
lines.speaker: Petruchio
lines.gloss: Not even whole cloth — an offcut.

lines.text: I wonder that you will still be talking, Signior Benedick: nobody marks you.
lines.speaker: Beatrice
lines.gloss: The opening shot of the merry war: you bore the room.

lines.text: What, my dear Lady Disdain! Are you yet living?
lines.speaker: Benedick
lines.gloss: Surprised she hasn't died of her own contempt.

lines.text: I had rather hear my dog bark at a crow than a man swear he loves me.
lines.speaker: Beatrice
lines.gloss: Ranks a barking dog above a wooing man.

lines.text: She speaks poniards, and every word stabs.
lines.speaker: Benedick
lines.gloss: Her sentences come to a point.

lines.text: I cannot endure my Lady Tongue.
lines.speaker: Benedick
lines.gloss: A whole woman renamed for her sharpest organ.

lines.text: Will you help? An ass-head, and a coxcomb, and a knave, a thin-faced knave, a gull!
lines.speaker: Sir Toby
lines.gloss: Four names for a fool, piled on a friend.

lines.text: Dost thou think, because thou art virtuous, there shall be no more cakes and ale?
lines.speaker: Sir Toby
lines.gloss: The eternal retort of fun to the killjoy.

lines.text: They have been at a great feast of languages, and stolen the scraps.
lines.speaker: Moth
lines.gloss: Big words, none of them earned.

lines.text: He draweth out the thread of his verbosity finer than the staple of his argument.
lines.speaker: Holofernes
lines.gloss: More words than meaning, spun thin.

lines.text: Thou halfpenny purse of wit, thou pigeon-egg of discretion!
lines.speaker: Costard
lines.gloss: Two tiny containers, both nearly empty.

lines.text: Some report a sea-maid spawned him; some, that he was begot between two stockfishes.
lines.speaker: Lucio
lines.gloss: Sired by dried fish; cold all the way down.

lines.text: You are not worth another word, else I'd call you knave.
lines.speaker: Lafew
lines.gloss: Too cheap even to insult properly.

lines.text: The soul of this man is his clothes.
lines.speaker: Lafew
lines.gloss: Nothing underneath the outfit.

lines.text: No, nor thy tailor, rascal, who is thy grandfather: he made those clothes, which make thee.
lines.speaker: Guiderius
lines.gloss: You are descended from your own outfit.

lines.text: You juggler! you canker-blossom! you thief of love!
lines.speaker: Hermia
lines.gloss: A cheat, a blight, and a love-thief in one breath.

lines.text: Fie, fie! you counterfeit, you puppet, you!
lines.speaker: Helena
lines.gloss: A little doll instead of a woman — which Hermia takes as a dig at her height.

lines.text: How low am I, thou painted maypole?
lines.speaker: Hermia
lines.gloss: Tall and over-made-up, like a decorated pole.

lines.text: Get you gone, you dwarf, you minimus, of hindering knot-grass made; you bead, you acorn!
lines.speaker: Lysander
lines.gloss: A cascade of the smallest things in the world.

lines.text: A mankind witch! Hence with her, out o' door: a most intelligencing bawd!
lines.speaker: Leontes
lines.gloss: A tyrant's slur at the one fearless woman in the room.

lines.text: She-wolf of France, but worse than wolves of France, whose tongue more poisons than the adder's tooth!
lines.speaker: York
lines.gloss: The Wakefield curse — predator and venom in one.

lines.text: O tiger's heart wrapped in a woman's hide!
lines.speaker: York
lines.gloss: Famous enough that Robert Greene parodied it at Shakespeare himself.

lines.text: Pole! Sir Pole! Lord! Ay, kennel, puddle, sink!
lines.speaker: the Lieutenant
lines.gloss: Punning a duke's name down into plumbing.

lines.text: Thou elvish-marked, abortive, rooting hog!
lines.speaker: Margaret
lines.gloss: The deformity-bestiary at full venom.

lines.text: Why strew'st thou sugar on that bottled spider?
lines.speaker: Margaret
lines.gloss: A swollen venom-sac with legs.

lines.text: Blush, blush, thou lump of foul deformity!
lines.speaker: Anne
lines.gloss: Over the corpse of the man he killed.

lines.text: You taught me language, and my profit on't is, I know how to curse.
lines.speaker: Caliban
lines.gloss: The keystone: a curse about cursing. (Also the pinned epigraph.)

lines.text: The red plague rid you for learning me your language!
lines.speaker: Caliban
lines.gloss: Disease wished on the man who taught him to speak.

lines.text: All the infections that the sun sucks up from bogs, fens, flats, on Prosper fall!
lines.speaker: Caliban
lines.gloss: The whole rotting marsh, summoned as a weapon.

lines.text: A south-west blow on ye and blister you all o'er!
lines.speaker: Caliban
lines.gloss: The wind itself enlisted to raise blisters.

lines.text: Thou poisonous slave, got by the devil himself!
lines.speaker: Prospero
lines.gloss: The master's contempt for the colonized.

lines.text: Either to be wooed with broad untuned oaths, or forced by rough insulting barbarism.
lines.speaker: the Countess of Salisbury
lines.gloss: The Scots' courtship: all crude oaths and rough force.

lines.text: Their wild, uncivil, skipping jigs bray forth their conquest and our overthrow.
lines.speaker: the Countess of Salisbury
lines.gloss: Their victory dance is just braying.
